title: The coherent cohomology bialgebra of a proper group
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $G$ be a proper geometrically integral group scheme over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Write $m:G\times_kG\to G$ and $e:\operatorname{Spec}k\to G$ for multiplication and identity. Put $H^n=H^n(G,\mathcal O_G)$, with Zariski module cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology, def-sc-field-linear-module-cohomology-operations], and $H=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}H^n$. Cup product and the structure map make $H$ a unital associative graded $k$-algebra, with $H^0=k\cdot1$ and $xy=(-1)^{pq}yx$ for $x\in H^p$, $y\in H^q$. The external cup-product map $\kappa:H\otimes_kH\to\bigoplus_n H^n(G\times_kG,\mathcal O_{G\times G})$ is an isomorphism of graded algebras, when the source has the signed multiplication $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=(-1)^{\deg b\deg c}ac\otimes bd$. The map $\Delta=\kappa^{-1}m^*:H\to H\otimes_kH$ is degree preserving, unital, multiplicative, and coassociative. Projection $\varepsilon:H\to H^0=k$ is its counit: $(\varepsilon\otimes1)\Delta=(1\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta=1_H$, under the tensor-unit identifications. In particular every $x\in H^1$ is primitive: $\Delta(x)=x\otimes1+1\otimes x$.

source.place: Tag 0BED, lemma-kunneth (external cup-product isomorphism), together with the group-law construction immediately preceding Milne AV I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55. The latter is written for etale cohomology; here the same construction uses Zariski coherent Kunneth and the cup product. This is an agent adaptation, not a claim that Milne states the coherent version verbatim. Cup signs and associativity: cohomology.tex, the cup-product construction and its graded-commutativity calculation.

proof.text: Geometric integrality gives geometric reducedness and connectedness: after every field extension the scheme is reduced and irreducible; a separation into two nonempty clopen sets contradicts irreducibility. Thus [lem-pc-h0-geom-connected] identifies the structure homomorphism $k\to H^0(G,\mathcal O_G)$ with an isomorphism. Properness gives finite type and a closed diagonal. Hence $G$ is quasi-compact over the affine base and its diagonal is affine. For $P=G\times_kG$, the projection to $G$ is proper by base change and $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper by composition. The same applies to $G^3$. They too are quasi-compact with affine diagonals: a closed immersion is affine by its affine-open quotient-ring description. These are exactly the geometric hypotheses needed for every Kunneth application below.

Write $A_X=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}H_k^n(X,\mathcal O_X)$ for each of $X=G,P,G^3$. Compose the coefficient cup with $\mathcal O_X\otimes\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_X$, $s\otimes t\mapsto st$. The associator, symmetry and unit identities of [lem-sfb-module-cup-associativity-symmetry-unit] give $(xy)z=x(yz)$, $xy=(-1)^{pq}yx$, and $1x=x1=x$. Bilinearity extends the pairings to the direct sum since every element has finite support. The scalar action is multiplication by the degree-zero constant class. Thus these are unital associative graded $k$-algebras, and step 1 gives $A_G^0=k\cdot1$. Cup/pullback coefficient naturality, applied to the structure-sheaf coefficient maps, makes every scheme pullback used below multiplicative. It preserves $1$: the degree-zero comparison identifies pullback of its class with pullback of the section $1$, and a unital structure-sheaf ring map sends $1$ to $1$. Scalar pullback agrees with ordinary module pullback; its identity is the cohomology map of the identity coefficient morphism and hence is the identity. Composition is the recorded scalar pullback composition law, with the canonical structure-sheaf coefficient identifications.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-picard-kunneth-qcoh] to $G,G$ with both coefficients the structure sheaf, which is quasi-coherent since on an affine chart it is the sheaf associated to its coordinate ring. Identify the external coefficient with $\mathcal O_P$ using pullback of the structure sheaf and the tensor unit. In each degree this gives the bijection $\kappa(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{pr}_1^*a\smile\operatorname{pr}_2^*b$. The direct-sum map is therefore bijective. For homogeneous $a,b,c,d$, associativity and swapping the middle two factors give $$\kappa(a\otimes b)\kappa(c\otimes d)=(-1)^{\deg b\deg c}\kappa(ac\otimes bd).$$ Both sides are bilinear, so this proves multiplicativity for the stated signed tensor multiplication; $\kappa(1\otimes1)=1$. That signed multiplication is associative because the two exponents for three pure tensors are $|b||c|+(|b|+|d|)|h|$ and $|d||h|+|b|(|c|+|h|)$ for factors $(a,b),(c,d),(h,j)$, and these are equal. Its unit is $1\otimes1$. Thus $\kappa$ is an isomorphism of graded algebras.

source.place: Tag 0BED, lemma-kunneth, projection-pullback definition of the canonical map; cup signs from cohomology.tex Tags 0FP4 and 0FP5

proof.text: Define $\Delta=\kappa^{-1}m^*$. Scheme cohomology pullback and $\kappa$ preserve degrees, so $\Delta$ does too. The algebra identities proved in steps 2 and 3 imply $\Delta(1)=1\otimes1$ and $\Delta(xy)=\Delta(x)\Delta(y)$, with exactly the signed tensor multiplication of step 3. This is transport through the explicitly defined external-product map, rather than an unspecified vector-space isomorphism.

source.place: Chapter I, printed p.55 (PDF p.61), group-law construction immediately before Lemma 12.2; agent adaptation to coherent Zariski cohomology using Tag 0BED

proof.text: Iterating Kunneth gives a bijection $K_3:H\otimes H\otimes H\to A_{G^3}$ taking $a\otimes b\otimes c$ to $p_1^*a\smile p_2^*b\smile p_3^*c$. The two parenthesizations agree: functoriality of projection pullbacks and cup associativity give this same formula on each pure tensor; pure tensors span. External-cup pullback compatibility applied to $(m,1_G)$ gives $$K_3(\Delta\otimes1)=(m\times1_G)^*\kappa,$$ since its value on $a\otimes b$ is the external product of $m^*a$ and $b$; expand $m^*a=\kappa\Delta(a)$ and use the displayed triple-product formula. Applying compatibility to $(1_G,m)$ gives $K_3(1\otimes\Delta)=(1_G\times m)^*\kappa$. Consequently the two iterated coproducts, followed by $K_3$, are respectively $(m\circ(m\times1_G))^*$ and $(m\circ(1_G\times m))^*$. The group associativity diagram identifies these maps. Cancel the bijection $K_3$ to obtain coassociativity, with the tensor associator understood.

source.place: Chapter I, printed p.55 (PDF p.61), group-law construction immediately before Lemma 12.2; agent adaptation to coherent Zariski cohomology using Tag 0BED

proof.text: For $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, affine vanishing gives $H^q(s,\mathcal O_s)=0$ for $q>0$, and degree zero is $k$. Thus $e^*:H\to A_s=k$ is the stated projection $\varepsilon$: in degree zero it is the inverse of the structure map because their composite is the identity on $s$, and in positive degrees its target is zero. Put $i_R=(1_G,e\circ\pi)$ and $i_L=(e\circ\pi,1_G)$, where $\pi:G\to s$. On a homogeneous pure tensor, cup naturality and pullback composition give $$i_R^*\kappa(a\otimes b)=a\smile\pi^*e^*b=\varepsilon(b)a,\qquad i_L^*\kappa(a\otimes b)=\pi^*e^*a\smile b=\varepsilon(a)b.$$ Here positive-degree factors pulled through $s$ vanish; degree-zero factors are constants and the two unit identities apply. By linearity these are $1\otimes\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon\otimes1$. The group unit diagrams say $m i_R=m i_L=1_G$, so composing with $\Delta$ gives both counit equations.

source.place: Chapter I, printed p.55 (PDF p.61), group-law construction immediately before Lemma 12.2; agent adaptation to coherent Zariski cohomology using Tag 0BED

proof.text: For $x\in H^1$, degree preservation puts $\Delta(x)$ in $(H^1\otimes H^0)\oplus(H^0\otimes H^1)$. Since $H^0=k\cdot1$, there are unique $a,b\in H^1$ with $\Delta(x)=a\otimes1+1\otimes b$. Applying $1\otimes\varepsilon$ gives $a=x$, because $\varepsilon$ is zero in degree one and $\varepsilon(1)=1$. Applying $\varepsilon\otimes1$ gives $b=x$. Hence $\Delta(x)=x\otimes1+1\otimes x$. No restriction on the characteristic was used.
